hook: Russia spans 11 time zones.
fact: Russia is so vast that when it's morning in Kaliningrad on its western edge, it's already the middle of the night in Kamchatka on its eastern edge.

fr.hook: La Russie s'étend sur 11 fuseaux horaires.
fr.fact: La Russie est si vaste que lorsqu'il est le matin à Kaliningrad, à l'extrémité occidentale du pays, il est déjà le milieu de la nuit au Kamtchatka, à l'extrémité orientale.

nl.hook: Rusland beslaat 11 tijdzones.
nl.fact: Rusland is zo uitgestrekt dat het al midden in de nacht is in Kamtsjatka aan de oostgrens, terwijl het in Kaliningrad aan de westgrens nog ochtend is.

es.hook: Rusia abarca 11 husos horarios.
es.fact: Rusia es tan extensa que cuando amanece en Kaliningrado, en su extremo occidental, ya es plena madrugada en Kamchatka, en su extremo oriental.

hook: Africa is bigger than most maps show.
fact: Because the standard Mercator map projection distorts size near the poles, Africa is actually large enough to fit the United States, China, India, and much of Europe inside it.

fr.hook: L'Afrique est plus grande que ce que montrent la plupart des cartes.
fr.fact: Comme la projection de Mercator déforme les tailles près des pôles, l'Afrique est en réalité assez vaste pour contenir les États-Unis, la Chine, l'Inde et une grande partie de l'Europe.

nl.hook: Afrika is groter dan de meeste kaarten laten zien.
nl.fact: Omdat de gangbare Mercatorprojectie de grootte bij de polen vervormt, is Afrika in werkelijkheid groot genoeg om de Verenigde Staten, China, India en een groot deel van Europa te bevatten.

es.hook: África es más grande de lo que muestran la mayoría de los mapas.
es.fact: Como la proyección de Mercator distorsiona el tamaño cerca de los polos, África es en realidad lo bastante grande como para contener a Estados Unidos, China, India y buena parte de Europa.

hook: There's a desert made of ice.
fact: Antarctica is technically the largest desert in the world — deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat, and Antarctica receives very little snowfall in its driest regions.

fr.hook: Il existe un désert entièrement fait de glace.
fr.fact: L'Antarctique est techniquement le plus grand désert du monde — un désert se définit par de faibles précipitations, pas par la chaleur, et l'Antarctique reçoit très peu de neige dans ses régions les plus sèches.

nl.hook: Er bestaat een woestijn van ijs.
nl.fact: Antarctica is technisch gezien de grootste woestijn ter wereld — woestijnen worden bepaald door weinig neerslag, niet door hitte, en Antarctica krijgt in zijn droogste gebieden nauwelijks sneeuwval.

es.hook: Existe un desierto hecho de hielo.
es.fact: La Antártida es, técnicamente, el desierto más grande del mundo: los desiertos se definen por la escasa precipitación, no por el calor, y la Antártida recibe muy poca nieve en sus regiones más secas.

hook: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.
fact: Canada contains an estimated 2 million lakes, accounting for roughly 60% of the world's total — a legacy of glaciers carving the landscape during the last ice age.

fr.hook: Le Canada compte plus de lacs que le reste du monde réuni.
fr.fact: Le Canada renferme environ 2 millions de lacs, soit près de 60% du total mondial — un héritage du façonnage du paysage par les glaciers lors de la dernière ère glaciaire.

nl.hook: Canada heeft meer meren dan de rest van de wereld samen.
nl.fact: Canada telt naar schatting 2 miljoen meren, goed voor ongeveer 60% van het wereldtotaal — een erfenis van gletsjers die het landschap tijdens de laatste ijstijd uitschuurden.

es.hook: Canadá tiene más lagos que el resto del mundo junto.
es.fact: Canadá alberga unos 2 millones de lagos, aproximadamente el 60% del total mundial, un legado de los glaciares que esculpieron el paisaje durante la última glaciación.

hook: Some countries are entirely surrounded by just one other country.
fact: Lesotho is completely enclosed within South Africa, and San Marino and Vatican City are entirely surrounded by Italy — a rare geographic setup called an 'enclave.'

fr.hook: Certains pays sont entièrement enclavés dans un seul autre pays.
fr.fact: Le Lesotho est complètement enclavé dans l'Afrique du Sud, tandis que Saint-Marin et le Vatican sont entièrement entourés par l'Italie — une configuration géographique rare appelée « enclave ».

nl.hook: Sommige landen liggen volledig binnen de grenzen van één ander land.
nl.fact: Lesotho ligt volledig ingesloten in Zuid-Afrika, en San Marino en Vaticaanstad worden helemaal omringd door Italië — een zeldzame geografische situatie die een 'enclave' wordt genoemd.

es.hook: Algunos países están completamente rodeados por un único país.
es.fact: Lesoto está totalmente rodeado por Sudáfrica, y San Marino y el Vaticano están completamente rodeados por Italia, una configuración geográfica poco común llamada 'enclave'.

hook: The Amazon rainforest produces a huge share of the world's oxygen.
fact: The Amazon generates an estimated 6–9% of the planet's oxygen and absorbs vast amounts of carbon dioxide, earning it the nickname 'the lungs of the Earth.'
whyItMatters: Deforestation there directly affects global climate regulation.

fr.hook: La forêt amazonienne produit une part énorme de l'oxygène mondial.
fr.fact: L'Amazonie génère environ 6 à 9% de l'oxygène de la planète et absorbe d'immenses quantités de dioxyde de carbone, ce qui lui a valu le surnom de « poumon de la Terre »।
fr.whyItMatters: La déforestation qui s'y produit affecte directement la régulation du climat mondial.

nl.hook: Het Amazonewoud produceert een enorm deel van 's werelds zuurstof.
nl.fact: De Amazone produceert naar schatting 6 tot 9% van de zuurstof op aarde en absorbeert enorme hoeveelheden kooldioxide, wat het de bijnaam 'de longen van de aarde' heeft opgeleverd.
nl.whyItMatters: Ontbossing daar heeft rechtstreeks invloed op de regulering van het wereldklimaat.

es.hook: La selva amazónica produce una enorme parte del oxígeno mundial.
es.fact: El Amazonas genera entre un 6% y un 9% del oxígeno del planeta y absorbe enormes cantidades de dióxido de carbono, lo que le ha valido el apodo de 'los pulmones de la Tierra'.
es.whyItMatters: La deforestación allí afecta directamente a la regulación del clima global.

hook: Mount Everest isn't the tallest mountain on Earth.
fact: Measured from base to peak rather than sea level, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is taller than Everest — most of it is just hidden underwater.

fr.hook: L'Everest n'est pas la plus haute montagne de la Terre.
fr.fact: Mesuré de la base au sommet plutôt qu'au niveau de la mer, le Mauna Kea, à Hawaï, est plus haut que l'Everest — la majeure partie est simplement cachée sous l'eau.

nl.hook: De Mount Everest is niet de hoogste berg op aarde.
nl.fact: Gemeten van basis tot top in plaats van vanaf zeeniveau, is de Mauna Kea op Hawaï hoger dan de Everest — het grootste deel ervan ligt gewoon verborgen onder water.

es.hook: El Everest no es la montaña más alta de la Tierra.
es.fact: Medido de base a cima en lugar de desde el nivel del mar, el Mauna Kea de Hawái es más alto que el Everest: la mayor parte simplemente está oculta bajo el agua.

hook: A river can flow in two different oceans.
fact: At Peru's Pasco region, a natural drainage divide splits water so closely that rain falling meters apart can end up flowing into either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean.

fr.hook: Une rivière peut se jeter dans deux océans différents.
fr.fact: Dans la région péruvienne de Pasco, une ligne de partage des eaux naturelle sépare l'eau de façon si étroite que des pluies tombées à quelques mètres d'écart peuvent finir dans l'Atlantique ou dans le Pacifique.

nl.hook: Een rivier kan in twee verschillende oceanen uitmonden.
nl.fact: In de Peruaanse regio Pasco scheidt een natuurlijke waterscheiding het water zo nauwkeurig dat regen die enkele meters uit elkaar valt, uiteindelijk in de Atlantische of de Stille Oceaan kan uitkomen.

es.hook: Un río puede desembocar en dos océanos distintos.
es.fact: En la región peruana de Pasco, una divisoria de aguas natural separa el agua con tanta precisión que la lluvia caída a pocos metros de distancia puede acabar fluyendo hacia el Atlántico o hacia el Pacífico.

hook: The Sahara wasn't always a desert.
fact: Around 6,000 years ago, the Sahara was a green savanna with lakes, rivers, and abundant wildlife, before a shift in Earth's orbit dried the region out over centuries.

fr.hook: Le Sahara n'a pas toujours été un désert.
fr.fact: Il y a environ 6 000 ans, le Sahara était une savane verdoyante parsemée de lacs, de rivières et d'une faune abondante, avant qu'un changement dans l'orbite terrestre n'assèche progressivement la région.

nl.hook: De Sahara was niet altijd een woestijn.
nl.fact: Zo'n 6.000 jaar geleden was de Sahara een groene savanne met meren, rivieren en een rijke fauna, tot een verschuiving in de omloopbaan van de aarde het gebied in de loop van eeuwen liet uitdrogen.

es.hook: El Sahara no siempre fue un desierto.
es.fact: Hace unos 6.000 años, el Sahara era una sabana verde con lagos, ríos y abundante fauna, antes de que un cambio en la órbita terrestre secara la región a lo largo de siglos.

hook: There's a country with no rivers at all.
fact: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers or lakes, relying instead on groundwater, desalination, and seasonal wadis that only fill after rare rainfall.

fr.hook: Il existe un pays sans le moindre fleuve.
fr.fact: L'Arabie saoudite ne compte aucun fleuve ni lac permanent, et dépend des eaux souterraines, du dessalement et des oueds saisonniers qui ne se remplissent qu'après de rares pluies.

nl.hook: Er is een land zonder één enkele rivier.
nl.fact: Saoedi-Arabië heeft geen permanente rivieren of meren en is aangewezen op grondwater, ontzilting en seizoensgebonden wadi's die alleen vollopen na zeldzame regenval.

es.hook: Hay un país sin un solo río.
es.fact: Arabia Saudí no tiene ríos ni lagos permanentes; depende de aguas subterráneas, desalinización y wadis estacionales que solo se llenan tras lluvias poco frecuentes.

hook: Indonesia is made up of over 17,000 islands.
fact: Indonesia's archipelago spans more than 17,000 islands, though only about 6,000 of them are inhabited.

fr.hook: L'Indonésie compte plus de 17 000 îles.
fr.fact: L'archipel indonésien s'étend sur plus de 17 000 îles, dont seulement environ 6 000 sont habitées.

nl.hook: Indonesië bestaat uit meer dan 17.000 eilanden.
nl.fact: De Indonesische archipel telt meer dan 17.000 eilanden, waarvan er slechts ongeveer 6.000 bewoond zijn.

es.hook: Indonesia está formada por más de 17.000 islas.
es.fact: El archipiélago indonesio abarca más de 17.000 islas, de las cuales solo unas 6.000 están habitadas.

hook: Chicago moved its entire downtown upward in the 1800s.
fact: In the 1850s–60s, engineers physically jacked up buildings in Chicago several feet using thousands of screw jacks to install proper sewage drainage below street level.

fr.hook: Chicago a soulevé tout son centre-ville au XIXe siècle.
fr.fact: Dans les années 1850-1860, des ingénieurs ont littéralement soulevé des bâtiments entiers de plusieurs mètres à Chicago à l'aide de milliers de vérins à vis, afin d'installer un système d'égouts sous le niveau de la rue.

nl.hook: Chicago tilde in de 19e eeuw zijn hele centrum op.
nl.fact: In de jaren 1850-1860 tilden ingenieurs in Chicago gebouwen met duizenden schroefvijzels enkele meters omhoog om onder straatniveau een fatsoenlijk rioleringssysteem aan te leggen.

es.hook: Chicago levantó todo su centro urbano en el siglo XIX.
es.fact: En las décadas de 1850 y 1860, los ingenieros levantaron físicamente edificios enteros de Chicago varios metros con miles de gatos de tornillo para instalar un sistema de alcantarillado bajo el nivel de la calle.

hook: The Dead Sea is dropping about a meter a year.
fact: Reduced inflow from the Jordan River and heavy mineral extraction cause the Dead Sea's water level to fall roughly one meter annually, shrinking its shoreline dramatically.

fr.hook: La mer Morte baisse d'environ un mètre par an.
fr.fact: La diminution des apports du Jourdain et l'extraction intensive de minéraux font baisser le niveau de la mer Morte d'environ un mètre par an, réduisant considérablement son littoral.

nl.hook: De Dode Zee daalt jaarlijks met ongeveer een meter.
nl.fact: Door een verminderde toevoer vanuit de Jordaan en intensieve mineralenwinning daalt het waterpeil van de Dode Zee jaarlijks met ongeveer een meter, waardoor de oever drastisch krimpt.

es.hook: El Mar Muerto desciende cerca de un metro al año.
es.fact: La reducción del caudal del río Jordán y la intensa extracción de minerales hacen que el nivel del Mar Muerto baje aproximadamente un metro al año, reduciendo drásticamente su litoral.

hook: There's a spot where four countries almost meet.
fact: Southern Africa's 'Four Corners' near Zambia, Zimbabwe, Botswana, and Namibia comes remarkably close to a true quadripoint, though surveys confirm they meet at two very close tripoints rather than one exact point.

fr.hook: Il existe un endroit où quatre pays se touchent presque.
fr.fact: Le « carrefour des quatre » dans le sud de l'Afrique, près de la Zambie, du Zimbabwe, du Botswana et de la Namibie, s'approche remarquablement d'un véritable quadripoint, bien que les relevés confirment qu'ils se rejoignent en deux tripoints très proches plutôt qu'en un seul point exact.

nl.hook: Er is een plek waar vier landen elkaar bijna raken.
nl.fact: De 'Four Corners' in zuidelijk Afrika, bij Zambia, Zimbabwe, Botswana en Namibië, komt opmerkelijk dicht bij een echt viervoudig grenspunt, al bevestigen metingen dat ze elkaar op twee zeer dicht bij elkaar liggende drielandenpunten raken in plaats van op één exact punt.

es.hook: Hay un lugar donde casi se encuentran cuatro países.
es.fact: Las 'Cuatro Esquinas' del sur de África, cerca de Zambia, Zimbabue, Botsuana y Namibia, se acercan mucho a un verdadero punto cuádruple, aunque los estudios confirman que en realidad se unen en dos puntos triples muy próximos entre sí, no en un único punto exacto.

hook: Mount Everest's official height changed by 86 centimeters in 2020.
fact: Nepal and China jointly re-measured Mount Everest using modern GPS technology and set its new official height at 8,848.86 meters — about 86 centimeters taller than the previously accepted figure.

fr.hook: L'altitude officielle de l'Everest a changé de 86 centimètres en 2020.
fr.fact: Le Népal et la Chine ont remesuré conjointement le mont Everest à l'aide de technologies GPS modernes et fixé sa nouvelle altitude officielle à 8 848,86 mètres — environ 86 centimètres de plus que le chiffre précédemment admis.

nl.hook: De officiële hoogte van de Mount Everest veranderde in 2020 met 86 centimeter.
nl.fact: Nepal en China hebben de Mount Everest samen opnieuw opgemeten met moderne gps-technologie en stelden de nieuwe officiële hoogte vast op 8.848,86 meter — ongeveer 86 centimeter hoger dan het eerder aanvaarde cijfer.

es.hook: La altura oficial del Everest cambió 86 centímetros en 2020.
es.fact: Nepal y China volvieron a medir conjuntamente el monte Everest con tecnología GPS moderna y fijaron su nueva altura oficial en 8.848,86 metros, unos 86 centímetros más que la cifra aceptada anteriormente.

hook: Australia's longest fence stretches over 5,600 kilometers.
fact: The Dingo Fence was built to keep dingoes away from sheep grazing land in southeastern Australia, and remains one of the longest structures ever built by humans.

fr.hook: La plus longue clôture d'Australie s'étend sur plus de 5 600 kilomètres.
fr.fact: La « Dingo Fence » a été construite pour tenir les dingos à l'écart des pâturages du sud-est de l'Australie, et reste l'une des plus longues structures jamais construites par l'homme.

nl.hook: Australiës langste hek is meer dan 5.600 kilometer lang.
nl.fact: Het Dingo Fence werd gebouwd om dingo's weg te houden van schapenweiden in het zuidoosten van Australië en blijft een van de langste bouwwerken die de mens ooit heeft opgetrokken.

es.hook: La valla más larga de Australia se extiende más de 5.600 kilómetros.
es.fact: La 'Dingo Fence' se construyó para mantener a los dingos alejados de los pastos ovinos del sureste de Australia, y sigue siendo una de las estructuras más largas jamás construidas por el ser humano.

hook: New Zealand was one of the last places on Earth settled by humans.
fact: Polynesian voyagers first reached New Zealand around 1250–1300 CE, making it one of the final major landmasses to be settled — thousands of years after most of the world.

fr.hook: La Nouvelle-Zélande a été l'un des derniers endroits du monde peuplés par l'homme.
fr.fact: Des navigateurs polynésiens ont atteint la Nouvelle-Zélande vers 1250-1300 apr. J.-C., ce qui en fait l'une des dernières grandes terres émergées à avoir été colonisées — des millénaires après la majeure partie du monde.

nl.hook: Nieuw-Zeeland was een van de laatste plekken op aarde die door mensen werden bewoond.
nl.fact: Polynesische zeevaarders bereikten Nieuw-Zeeland rond 1250-1300 n.Chr., waarmee het een van de laatste grote landmassa's is die werd bewoond — duizenden jaren na de rest van de wereld.

es.hook: Nueva Zelanda fue uno de los últimos lugares del mundo poblados por el ser humano.
es.fact: Navegantes polinesios llegaron a Nueva Zelanda hacia el 1250-1300 d.C., lo que la convierte en una de las últimas grandes masas de tierra en ser pobladas, miles de años después que la mayor parte del mundo.

hook: South America has only two landlocked countries.
fact: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only two countries in South America without direct ocean access, despite the continent's long coastlines.

fr.hook: L'Amérique du Sud ne compte que deux pays enclavés.
fr.fact: La Bolivie et le Paraguay sont les deux seuls pays d'Amérique du Sud sans accès direct à l'océan, malgré les longues côtes du continent.

nl.hook: Zuid-Amerika telt slechts twee landlocked landen.
nl.fact: Bolivia en Paraguay zijn de enige twee landen in Zuid-Amerika zonder rechtstreekse toegang tot de oceaan, ondanks de lange kustlijnen van het continent.

es.hook: Sudamérica solo tiene dos países sin salida al mar.
es.fact: Bolivia y Paraguay son los únicos países de Sudamérica sin acceso directo al océano, pese a las largas costas del continente.

hook: The Amazon carries more water than the next seven biggest rivers combined.
fact: The Amazon River's flow into the Atlantic Ocean is so massive that it outpaces the combined discharge of the next seven largest rivers on Earth.

fr.hook: L'Amazone transporte plus d'eau que les sept plus grands fleuves suivants réunis.
fr.fact: Le débit de l'Amazone dans l'océan Atlantique est si colossal qu'il dépasse le débit combiné des sept plus grands fleuves suivants de la planète.

nl.hook: De Amazone voert meer water af dan de zeven op één na grootste rivieren samen.
nl.fact: De afvoer van de Amazone naar de Atlantische Oceaan is zo enorm dat die groter is dan de gecombineerde afvoer van de zeven op één na grootste rivieren ter wereld.

es.hook: El Amazonas lleva más agua que los siete ríos siguientes más grandes juntos.
es.fact: El caudal del río Amazonas hacia el océano Atlántico es tan colosal que supera al caudal combinado de los siete ríos más grandes que le siguen en la Tierra.

hook: Singapore has grown its land area by over 20% since independence.
fact: Through decades of land reclamation projects, Singapore has expanded its total land area by more than a fifth since becoming independent in 1965.

fr.hook: Singapour a agrandi sa superficie de plus de 20% depuis son indépendance.
fr.fact: Grâce à des décennies de projets de poldérisation, Singapour a étendu sa superficie totale de plus d'un cinquième depuis son indépendance en 1965.

nl.hook: Singapore is sinds de onafhankelijkheid meer dan 20% in landoppervlakte gegroeid.
nl.fact: Dankzij decennia van landaanwinningsprojecten heeft Singapore zijn totale landoppervlakte sinds de onafhankelijkheid in 1965 met meer dan een vijfde uitgebreid.

es.hook: Singapur ha aumentado su superficie más de un 20% desde su independencia.
es.fact: Gracias a décadas de proyectos de recuperación de tierra al mar, Singapur ha ampliado su superficie total en más de una quinta parte desde que se independizó en 1965.

hook: There's a point on Earth more than 2,600 km from any ocean.
fact: Located in northwestern China, the 'Eurasian pole of inaccessibility' is the spot on Earth's surface farthest from any coastline in every direction.

fr.hook: Il existe un point sur Terre à plus de 2 600 km de tout océan.
fr.fact: Situé dans le nord-ouest de la Chine, le « pôle continental d'inaccessibilité » est l'endroit de la surface terrestre le plus éloigné de toute côte, dans toutes les directions.

nl.hook: Er is een plek op aarde die meer dan 2.600 km van elke oceaan verwijderd is.
nl.fact: De 'continentale onbereikbaarheidspool', gelegen in het noordwesten van China, is het punt op het aardoppervlak dat in elke richting het verst van een kustlijn verwijderd ligt.

es.hook: Hay un punto en la Tierra a más de 2.600 km de cualquier océano.
es.fact: Situado en el noroeste de China, el 'polo continental de inaccesibilidad' es el punto de la superficie terrestre más alejado de cualquier costa en todas las direcciones.

hook: Iceland is icier in name than in reality — and Greenland is the opposite.
fact: Iceland is only about 10% covered in glaciers, while much of Greenland's southern coast is comparatively green — a naming mismatch that traces back to medieval Norse settlers.

fr.hook: L'Islande est plus glacée de nom que de fait — et le Groenland, c'est l'inverse.
fr.fact: L'Islande n'est couverte de glaciers qu'à environ 10%, tandis qu'une grande partie de la côte sud du Groenland est relativement verte — une inversion de noms qui remonte aux colons scandinaves médiévaux.

nl.hook: IJsland is ijziger van naam dan in werkelijkheid — en bij Groenland is het net andersom.
nl.fact: IJsland is voor slechts ongeveer 10% bedekt met gletsjers, terwijl een groot deel van de zuidkust van Groenland relatief groen is — een naamverwarring die teruggaat op middeleeuwse Noorse kolonisten.

es.hook: Islandia es más helada de nombre que en la realidad, y con Groenlandia pasa justo lo contrario.
es.fact: Islandia solo está cubierta de glaciares en un 10% aproximadamente, mientras que buena parte de la costa sur de Groenlandia es relativamente verde, una confusión de nombres que se remonta a los colonos nórdicos medievales.

hook: The Nile might not be the longest river after all.
fact: The Nile has long been considered the world's longest river, but some modern measurements suggest the Amazon could actually be longer, depending on exactly where its source is defined.

fr.hook: Le Nil n'est peut-être pas le plus long fleuve du monde, finalement.
fr.fact: Le Nil est depuis longtemps considéré comme le plus long fleuve du monde, mais certaines mesures modernes suggèrent que l'Amazone pourrait en réalité être plus long, selon l'endroit exact où l'on situe sa source.

nl.hook: De Nijl is misschien toch niet de langste rivier ter wereld.
nl.fact: De Nijl wordt al lang beschouwd als de langste rivier ter wereld, maar sommige moderne metingen suggereren dat de Amazone eigenlijk langer zou kunnen zijn, afhankelijk van waar precies de bron wordt gedefinieerd.

es.hook: Puede que el Nilo no sea, después de todo, el río más largo.
es.fact: El Nilo se ha considerado durante mucho tiempo el río más largo del mundo, pero algunas mediciones modernas sugieren que el Amazonas podría ser en realidad más largo, dependiendo de dónde se defina exactamente su nacimiento.

hook: There's a patch of desert no country wants to claim.
fact: Bir Tawil, a strip of land between Egypt and Sudan, is unclaimed by either country — claiming it would weaken each nation's position in a separate, more valuable border dispute nearby.

fr.hook: Il existe un morceau de désert qu'aucun pays ne veut revendiquer.
fr.fact: Bir Tawil, une bande de terre entre l'Égypte et le Soudan, n'est revendiquée par aucun des deux pays — la revendiquer affaiblirait la position de chaque nation dans un différend frontalier voisin bien plus précieux.

nl.hook: Er ligt een stuk woestijn dat geen enkel land wil opeisen.
nl.fact: Bir Tawil, een stuk land tussen Egypte en Soedan, wordt door geen van beide landen opgeëist — het opeisen ervan zou de positie van elk land verzwakken in een ander, waardevoller grensgeschil in de buurt.

es.hook: Hay un trozo de desierto que ningún país quiere reclamar.
es.fact: Bir Tawil, una franja de tierra entre Egipto y Sudán, no es reclamada por ninguno de los dos países: reclamarla debilitaría la posición de cada nación en una disputa fronteriza cercana mucho más valiosa.

hook: Japan has more than double the islands it was once thought to have.
fact: A 2023 government recount using precise digital mapping revised Japan's official island count from 6,852 to 14,125.

fr.hook: Le Japon compte plus du double des îles qu'on lui attribuait autrefois.
fr.fact: Un recensement gouvernemental de 2023, réalisé grâce à une cartographie numérique précise, a révisé le nombre officiel d'îles du Japon, le faisant passer de 6 852 à 14 125.

nl.hook: Japan heeft meer dan dubbel zoveel eilanden als tot voor kort werd gedacht.
nl.fact: Een Japanse overheidstelling uit 2023, uitgevoerd met precieze digitale cartografie, herzag het officiële eilandenaantal van Japan van 6.852 naar 14.125.

es.hook: Japón tiene más del doble de islas de las que se pensaba.
es.fact: Un recuento gubernamental de 2023, realizado con cartografía digital de precisión, revisó la cifra oficial de islas de Japón de 6.852 a 14.125.

hook: Parts of Chile's Atacama Desert have never recorded rain.
fact: The Atacama is considered the driest inhabited place on Earth — some of its weather stations have no recorded rainfall in their entire history of operation.

fr.hook: Certaines parties du désert d'Atacama, au Chili, n'ont jamais enregistré de pluie.
fr.fact: L'Atacama est considéré comme l'endroit habité le plus sec de la planète — certaines de ses stations météo n'ont enregistré aucune précipitation depuis leur mise en service.

nl.hook: In delen van de Atacamawoestijn in Chili is nog nooit regen geregistreerd.
nl.fact: De Atacama geldt als de droogste bewoonde plek op aarde — sommige weerstations daar hebben in hun hele bestaan nog nooit neerslag geregistreerd.

es.hook: En partes del desierto de Atacama, en Chile, nunca se ha registrado lluvia.
es.fact: El Atacama se considera el lugar habitado más seco de la Tierra: algunas de sus estaciones meteorológicas no han registrado precipitación alguna en toda su historia de funcionamiento.

hook: Vatican City is smaller than most golf courses.
fact: The world's smallest country covers just 0.49 square kilometers, making it tinier than the average 18-hole golf course.

fr.hook: Le Vatican est plus petit que la plupart des terrains de golf.
fr.fact: Le plus petit pays du monde couvre à peine 0,49 kilomètre carré, ce qui le rend plus petit qu'un terrain de golf moyen de 18 trous.

nl.hook: Vaticaanstad is kleiner dan de meeste golfbanen.
nl.fact: Het kleinste land ter wereld beslaat slechts 0,49 vierkante kilometer, waardoor het kleiner is dan een gemiddelde golfbaan met 18 holes.

es.hook: El Vaticano es más pequeño que la mayoría de los campos de golf.
es.fact: El país más pequeño del mundo ocupa apenas 0,49 kilómetros cuadrados, lo que lo hace más pequeño que un campo de golf medio de 18 hoyos.

hook: Australia is the only continent-spanning country with no land borders.
fact: Because it's surrounded entirely by ocean, Australia is the sole country that covers an entire continent while sharing a land border with absolutely no other nation.

fr.hook: L'Australie est le seul pays-continent sans aucune frontière terrestre.
fr.fact: Entièrement entourée par l'océan, l'Australie est le seul pays à couvrir un continent entier tout en ne partageant de frontière terrestre avec absolument aucune autre nation.

nl.hook: Australië is het enige land dat een heel continent beslaat zonder landgrenzen.
nl.fact: Omdat het volledig door oceaan wordt omringd, is Australië het enige land dat een heel continent beslaat en tegelijk met geen enkel ander land een landgrens deelt.

es.hook: Australia es el único país-continente sin fronteras terrestres.
es.fact: Al estar completamente rodeada por el océano, Australia es el único país que ocupa un continente entero sin compartir frontera terrestre con ninguna otra nación.

hook: Geographers still argue about whether the Caspian is a sea or a lake.
fact: The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water on Earth, and whether it technically counts as a sea or the world's biggest lake remains a genuine debate among geographers.

fr.hook: Les géographes se disputent encore pour savoir si la mer Caspienne est une mer ou un lac.
fr.fact: La mer Caspienne est la plus grande étendue d'eau intérieure de la planète, et la question de savoir si elle constitue techniquement une mer ou le plus grand lac du monde reste un véritable débat parmi les géographes.

nl.hook: Geografen twisten nog altijd of de Kaspische Zee een zee of een meer is.
nl.fact: De Kaspische Zee is het grootste binnenwater ter wereld, en of het technisch gezien als een zee of als 's werelds grootste meer geldt, blijft een echt discussiepunt onder geografen.

es.hook: Los geógrafos todavía discuten si el Caspio es un mar o un lago.
es.fact: El mar Caspio es la mayor masa de agua interior del planeta, y si técnicamente cuenta como mar o como el lago más grande del mundo sigue siendo un debate real entre geógrafos.

hook: Kilimanjaro is the tallest mountain that isn't part of a range.
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the world's tallest freestanding mountain, rising on its own rather than as part of a larger mountain chain.

fr.hook: Le Kilimandjaro est la plus haute montagne qui ne fasse partie d'aucune chaîne.
fr.fact: Le mont Kilimandjaro, en Tanzanie, est la plus haute montagne isolée du monde, s'élevant seule plutôt que comme partie d'une chaîne montagneuse plus vaste.

nl.hook: De Kilimanjaro is de hoogste berg die geen deel uitmaakt van een gebergte.
nl.fact: De Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is de hoogste alleenstaande berg ter wereld, die op zichzelf oprijst in plaats van als onderdeel van een groter gebergte.

es.hook: El Kilimanjaro es la montaña más alta que no forma parte de una cordillera.
es.fact: El monte Kilimanjaro, en Tanzania, es la montaña independiente más alta del mundo, que se eleva por sí sola en lugar de formar parte de una cadena montañosa mayor.

hook: The Chile–Argentina border runs over 5,300 kilometers along the Andes.
fact: One of the longest international borders on Earth follows the spine of the Andes mountains between Chile and Argentina, stretching more than 5,300 kilometers.

fr.hook: La frontière entre le Chili et l'Argentine s'étend sur plus de 5 300 kilomètres le long des Andes.
fr.fact: L'une des plus longues frontières internationales du monde suit la ligne de crête des Andes entre le Chili et l'Argentine, s'étendant sur plus de 5 300 kilomètres.

nl.hook: De grens tussen Chili en Argentinië loopt meer dan 5.300 kilometer langs de Andes.
nl.fact: Een van de langste internationale grenzen ter wereld volgt de bergkam van de Andes tussen Chili en Argentinië, en strekt zich uit over meer dan 5.300 kilometer.

es.hook: La frontera entre Chile y Argentina recorre más de 5.300 kilómetros a lo largo de los Andes.
es.fact: Una de las fronteras internacionales más largas del mundo sigue la cordillera de los Andes entre Chile y Argentina, extendiéndose a lo largo de más de 5.300 kilómetros.

hook: Africa is slowly tearing itself in two.
fact: The East African Rift is a 6,000-kilometer crack where the African continent is splitting apart at roughly the speed fingernails grow. In millions of years, the region will likely become a new ocean basin, separating a new landmass from the rest of Africa.

hook: One lake holds a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.
fact: Siberia's Lake Baikal is both the deepest (over 1,600 meters) and oldest (roughly 25 million years) freshwater lake on Earth, and it alone contains about 20% of the planet's unfrozen surface fresh water.

hook: Water falls nearly a kilometer before it hits anything.
fact: Venezuela's Angel Falls drops 979 meters in a single uninterrupted plunge from the edge of a flat-topped tepui mountain, making it the tallest waterfall on Earth. Much of the water evaporates or scatters into mist before reaching the bottom.

hook: People live in one of the hottest places on the planet, on purpose.
fact: Ethiopia's Danakil Depression regularly sees average temperatures among the highest recorded anywhere on Earth, yet Afar salt miners still work its blistering, sulfur-streaked salt flats near active volcanic vents.

hook: Yellowstone Park sits on top of one giant volcano.
fact: The geysers and hot springs of Yellowstone are powered by a supervolcano whose caldera spans roughly 70 kilometers across, formed by eruptions so massive they buried much of North America in ash.

hook: The Grand Canyon's walls are a time machine.
fact: Erosion by the Colorado River has cut so deep that rock at the canyon's base dates back nearly 2 billion years — close to half the age of Earth itself.

hook: Most of the Sahara isn't actually covered in sand dunes.
fact: Only about 15% of the Sahara is the rolling sand seas people picture. The rest is rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains — a much starker, harder landscape than the postcard image.

hook: There's a point in the ocean where the pressure could crush a car.
fact: At the bottom of the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, nearly 11 kilometers down, water pressure exceeds a thousand times what it is at the surface — yet specialized submersibles have still reached the bottom and found life.

hook: A sea in Central Asia lost most of itself in a few decades.
fact: The Aral Sea was once the world's fourth-largest lake, but Soviet-era irrigation projects diverted the rivers that fed it, shrinking it to a fraction of its original size and leaving rusting fishing boats stranded in desert.
whyItMatters: The collapse devastated regional fisheries and left toxic, salt-laden dust storms that still affect public health across Central Asia.

hook: One reef is big enough to see from space.
fact: Australia's Great Barrier Reef stretches over 2,300 kilometers and is built entirely by tiny coral organisms, making it the largest structure on Earth constructed by living creatures.

hook: A giant rock in the desert changes color at sunset.
fact: Uluru, the massive sandstone monolith in central Australia, appears to glow deep red at dawn and dusk because iron minerals on its surface have oxidized, essentially rusting the rock's outer layer.

hook: Japan's most iconic mountain is still technically active.
fact: Mount Fuji's perfectly symmetrical cone last erupted in 1707–08, and volcanologists still classify it as an active volcano rather than dormant or extinct.

hook: One horseshoe-shaped zone holds most of Earth's volcanoes.
fact: The Pacific 'Ring of Fire' is home to roughly 75% of the world's active and dormant volcanoes and around 90% of its earthquakes, tracing the edges of the tectonic plates that ring the Pacific Ocean.

hook: The Appalachian Mountains are older than the ocean next to them.
fact: The Appalachians formed roughly 480 million years ago and were once part of the same range as mountains now found in Scotland and Scandinavia — long before the Atlantic Ocean, which is only about 180 million years old, ever existed.

hook: The Himalayas are getting taller every year.
fact: The Indian tectonic plate is still colliding with the Eurasian plate, pushing the Himalayas upward by a few millimeters annually — a slow-motion collision that has been happening for tens of millions of years.
whyItMatters: That same ongoing collision is why the region is one of the most earthquake-prone on Earth.

hook: Scientists call one plateau the 'Third Pole.'
fact: The Tibetan Plateau holds the largest store of ice outside the Arctic and Antarctic, feeding the headwaters of major rivers that supply water to nearly two billion people across Asia.

hook: There's a lake in the Andes boats can sail on at 3,800 meters up.
fact: Lake Titicaca, straddling the border of Peru and Bolivia, is the highest lake in the world navigable by large vessels, sitting so high that the air holds noticeably less oxygen than at sea level.

hook: One waterfall is actually about 275 waterfalls.
fact: Iguazu Falls, on the border of Argentina and Brazil, isn't a single cascade but a horseshoe-shaped system of roughly 275 individual falls and cataracts, making it significantly wider than Niagara Falls.

hook: One desert has been dry for tens of millions of years.
fact: Namibia's Namib Desert is considered the oldest desert on Earth, having remained arid for at least 55 to 80 million years — long enough to predate most mammal species alive today.

hook: A river delta in Africa never actually reaches the ocean.
fact: Botswana's Okavango Delta forms where a river flowing out of Angola's highlands spreads across the Kalahari Desert and simply evaporates or soaks into the sand, rather than draining into any sea.

hook: Locals call it 'the smoke that thunders.'
fact: Victoria Falls, on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border, produces a curtain of spray visible from kilometers away and is classified as the largest single sheet of falling water on Earth by combined height and width.

hook: One river crosses the equator not once, but twice.
fact: The Congo River loops so dramatically through central Africa that it crosses the equator twice, and it plunges to depths over 220 meters in places, making it the deepest river in the world.

hook: The hottest air temperature ever reliably recorded was in a valley below sea level.
fact: Death Valley, California, hit 56.7°C (134°F) at Furnace Creek in 1913 — the highest air temperature officially recorded on Earth's surface.

hook: One cave system has more mapped passages than any other on Earth.
fact: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky has over 675 kilometers of surveyed passageways, and explorers keep finding more, connecting it to nearby cave systems as mapping continues.

hook: Niagara Falls didn't start where it is today.
fact: Erosion has caused Niagara Falls to retreat several kilometers upstream from its original location near Lake Ontario over the past 12,000 years, as the rushing water wears away the rock beneath it.

hook: Five lakes hold about a fifth of the world's surface fresh water.
fact: North America's Great Lakes — Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario — together contain roughly 20% of all the fresh surface water on the planet.
whyItMatters: They supply drinking water to tens of millions of people across the US and Canada.

hook: There's a sea with no coastline at all.
fact: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is defined not by any shore but by the swirling ocean currents around it, making it the only sea on Earth bordered entirely by water rather than land.

hook: A single ocean current keeps entire countries warmer than they should be.
fact: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic toward Western Europe, which is why London stays far milder in winter than places at similar latitudes in North America.
whyItMatters: Some climate models suggest this circulation could slow down as polar ice melts, which would sharply cool parts of Europe.

hook: One Siberian village regularly hits temperatures cold enough to freeze exposed skin in minutes.
fact: Oymyakon, in northeastern Siberia, is widely considered the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth, with temperatures having dropped as low as -67.7°C.

hook: Almost all the world's ice sits on one continent.
fact: Antarctica holds roughly 90% of Earth's ice and about 70% of its fresh water, locked in an ice sheet that in places is several kilometers thick.
whyItMatters: If it all melted, global sea levels would rise by tens of meters, reshaping coastlines worldwide.

hook: There's a lake that hasn't seen sunlight in millions of years.
fact: Lake Vostok lies buried under nearly 4 kilometers of Antarctic ice, sealed off from the surface for possibly millions of years, giving scientists a rare window into an isolated ancient ecosystem.

hook: The world's second-highest mountain is also its deadliest to climb.
fact: K2 stands just shy of Everest in height, but its steep terrain, unpredictable weather, and technical climbing routes give it a far higher fatality rate, earning it the nickname 'the Savage Mountain.'

hook: One peninsula has one of the densest clusters of volcanoes on Earth.
fact: Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula is home to dozens of active volcanoes packed into a relatively small area, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire and recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

hook: Europe's most active volcano has been erupting for centuries.
fact: Mount Etna in Sicily is Europe's most active volcano, with a documented history of eruptions stretching back thousands of years and activity that continues to this day.

hook: Earth's longest mountain range is almost entirely underwater.
fact: The global mid-ocean ridge system stretches roughly 65,000 kilometers around the planet, making it the longest continuous mountain range on Earth — yet it's almost completely submerged beneath the oceans.

hook: One mountain range runs the entire length of a continent.
fact: The Andes stretch about 7,000 kilometers along the western edge of South America, making them the longest continental mountain range in the world.

hook: One forest holds roughly a tenth of all known species on Earth.
fact: The Amazon rainforest is estimated to harbor around 10% of the world's documented species, packed into an area covering less than 1% of Earth's surface.

hook: The world's largest tropical wetland isn't the Amazon.
fact: Brazil's Pantanal, extending into Bolivia and Paraguay, is the largest tropical wetland on Earth, spanning an area roughly the size of a small country and supporting extraordinary concentrations of wildlife.

hook: Outside the poles, one place holds more ice than anywhere else in the Southern Hemisphere.
fact: The Patagonian Ice Fields, spanning parts of Chile and Argentina, form the largest contiguous mass of ice in the Southern Hemisphere outside of Antarctica itself.

hook: An island chain that inspired evolutionary theory was never attached to any continent.
fact: The Galápagos Islands are entirely volcanic in origin, rising from a hotspot in the Pacific Ocean floor, and were never connected to mainland South America — which is why their wildlife evolved in such striking isolation.

hook: One river delta is the largest on the planet.
fact: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the largest river delta in the world, formed where sediment from the Himalayas spreads across a vast low-lying floodplain before reaching the Bay of Bengal.
whyItMatters: Tens of millions of people live on this delta, making it one of the most flood-vulnerable regions on Earth as sea levels rise.

hook: Asia's longest river starts as glacial meltwater on a remote plateau.
fact: The Yangtze River stretches about 6,300 kilometers from its source on the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea, making it the longest river in Asia and the third-longest in the world.

hook: One river flows through six different countries before reaching the sea.
fact: The Mekong River begins on the Tibetan Plateau and winds through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam, sustaining fisheries and farmland for tens of millions of people along the way.

hook: Not every desert is hot.
fact: Mongolia and northern China's Gobi Desert is classified as a cold desert, where winter temperatures regularly plunge well below freezing despite it receiving so little precipitation that it technically qualifies as arid.

hook: Some sand dunes stretch over 200 kilometers in a single line.
fact: Australia's Simpson Desert contains some of the longest parallel sand dunes on Earth, with individual dune ridges running for over 200 kilometers across the outback.

hook: A fifth of a continent sits above one giant underground water reserve.
fact: The Great Artesian Basin underlies about 22% of Australia, forming one of the largest and deepest freshwater aquifer systems on Earth and supplying water to remote communities across the arid interior.

hook: The line dividing Europe from Asia runs through a worn-down mountain range.
fact: The Ural Mountains, stretching through Russia, are conventionally treated as the physical boundary between Europe and Asia — and at roughly 250 to 300 million years old, they're far more eroded and gentle than younger ranges like the Alps.

hook: One Norwegian fjord plunges deeper than most skyscrapers are tall.
fact: Sognefjord, Norway's longest and deepest fjord, stretches about 205 kilometers inland and reaches depths over 1,300 meters, carved by glaciers during past ice ages.

hook: Mainland Europe has exactly one active volcano.
fact: Mount Vesuvius, near Naples, Italy, is the only active volcano on the European mainland, infamous for the 79 CE eruption that buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

hook: The Alps' tallest peak doesn't have a fixed height.
fact: Mont Blanc's elevation shifts slightly from year to year because its summit is capped by snow and ice whose thickness changes with the seasons, so surveyors periodically remeasure it.

hook: One river touches more countries than any other on Earth.
fact: The Danube flows through roughly ten countries on its way from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea, more than any other river in the world.

hook: No bridge crosses the world's second-longest river along its entire length.
fact: Despite stretching thousands of kilometers through dense rainforest, the Amazon River has no bridges spanning it anywhere along its course — settlements along its banks rely on boats and ferries instead.

hook: Two rivers with different colors meet in one African capital.
fact: The Blue Nile and White Nile visibly merge at Khartoum, Sudan, flowing side by side for a stretch before their waters — carrying different sediment loads — fully mix into a single Nile River.

hook: One African lake is both the world's second-deepest and one of its oldest.
fact: Lake Tanganyika plunges to depths over 1,400 meters and formed roughly 9 to 12 million years ago as part of the East African Rift system, making it both remarkably deep and remarkably old.

hook: Africa's largest lake by area feeds the world's longest river.
fact: Lake Victoria, shared by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania, is the largest lake in Africa by surface area and serves as one of the primary sources feeding the Nile River.

hook: One volcano has had a bubbling lava lake for over a century.
fact: Ethiopia's Erta Ale is one of only a handful of volcanoes on Earth with a persistent, long-lived lava lake in its summit crater, glowing continuously rather than erupting in a single burst.

hook: One mountain rises higher above its own base than almost any other on land.
fact: Alaska's Denali gains roughly 5,500 meters of vertical relief from its surrounding base to summit, entirely above sea level — giving it one of the greatest base-to-peak rises of any mountain on land.

hook: A single crack in California's crust can move an entire city.
fact: The San Andreas Fault marks where the Pacific and North American tectonic plates grind past each other, and its sudden slips have produced some of the most destructive earthquakes in US history.
whyItMatters: Millions of Californians live along the fault line, and geologists warn a major rupture is a matter of when, not if.

hook: One eruption blew off the top of a mountain in seconds.
fact: The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington State collapsed the volcano's north face and blasted away roughly 400 meters of its summit, in one of the most closely studied volcanic events in modern history.

hook: One geyser has been putting on a show for over a century, right on schedule.
fact: Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park erupts fairly predictably, roughly every hour or two, powered by heat from the supervolcano lurking beneath the park.

hook: North America's two great mountain ranges are millions of years apart in age.
fact: The Rocky Mountains formed only about 55 to 80 million years ago, making them far younger than the Appalachians on the continent's other coast, which are more than five times older.

hook: One river system drains nearly a third of the United States.
fact: The Mississippi River's watershed covers all or part of 31 US states, plus small portions of Canada, making it one of the largest drainage basins on Earth.

hook: One of Florida's defining features isn't a swamp — it's a river.
fact: The Everglades is technically a slow-moving, wide, shallow river, often called a 'river of grass,' flowing almost imperceptibly across a vast limestone shelf toward the sea.

hook: A quarter of the Northern Hemisphere's land sits on ground that never fully thaws.
fact: Permafrost underlies roughly a quarter of land in the Northern Hemisphere and locks away vast stores of ancient carbon that has been frozen for thousands of years.
whyItMatters: As permafrost thaws with rising temperatures, it can release that stored carbon as greenhouse gases, accelerating global warming further.

hook: Earth's largest land biome isn't a rainforest or a desert.
fact: The taiga, or boreal forest, forms a nearly unbroken band of coniferous trees across Russia, Scandinavia, Canada, and Alaska, making it the largest land biome on the planet by area.

hook: One biome covers both the Arctic and the tops of tropical mountains.
fact: Tundra, defined by permafrost and short growing seasons, isn't limited to polar regions — alpine tundra appears on high mountain slopes worldwide, wherever elevation mimics the cold of the far north.

hook: One grassland hosts the largest land mammal migration on Earth.
fact: East Africa's Serengeti ecosystem is a classic savanna biome, and each year roughly two million wildebeest, zebra, and gazelle migrate across it in search of fresh grazing and water.

hook: Some regions get almost all their yearly rainfall in just a few months.
fact: The South Asian monsoon is a seasonal reversal of wind patterns that delivers the vast majority of the region's annual rainfall in a concentrated summer window, shaping agriculture for over a billion people.

hook: Warmer water in one patch of the Pacific can shift weather worldwide.
fact: El Niño is a periodic warming of surface waters in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean that disrupts atmospheric circulation patterns, triggering droughts, floods, and temperature swings across multiple continents.
whyItMatters: El Niño events can devastate crop yields and fisheries in affected regions, making them a major factor in global food prices.

hook: Coral turns white when it's under stress, not when it dies.
fact: Coral bleaching happens when heat-stressed corals expel the colorful algae living in their tissue, leaving behind a stark white skeleton — the coral isn't dead yet, but it's starving and vulnerable.
whyItMatters: Repeated bleaching events, driven by warming oceans, threaten reef ecosystems that support roughly a quarter of all marine species.

hook: All of today's continents were once fused into a single landmass.
fact: Around 200 million years ago, the supercontinent Pangaea began splitting apart, and the pieces have been drifting into their current configuration ever since — a process that continues today.

hook: The ground beneath your feet is riding on a moving plate.
fact: Earth's outer shell is broken into large tectonic plates that drift atop the semi-molten mantle below, and their collisions, separations, and sideways grinding are what cause most earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain-building on the planet.

hook: We've mapped more of Mars than the bottom of our own oceans.
fact: The world's oceans average about 3,700 meters deep, and a large majority of the ocean floor remains unmapped in detail, even though satellite imagery has charted the surface of Mars far more thoroughly.

hook: One bay has the most extreme tides on the planet.
fact: Canada's Bay of Fundy experiences the highest tidal range in the world, with water levels differing by as much as 16 meters between high and low tide.

hook: There's a perfectly round hole in the ocean visible from a plane.
fact: The Great Blue Hole off the coast of Belize is a giant marine sinkhole about 300 meters across and over 120 meters deep, formed as a limestone cave that collapsed and flooded during past ice ages.

hook: One island is so isolated that a third of its plants exist nowhere else.
fact: Yemen's Socotra Island has been separated from the mainland for millions of years, allowing roughly a third of its plant species — including the umbrella-shaped dragon's blood tree — to evolve in complete isolation.

hook: One country is slowly ripping itself in half.
fact: Iceland sits directly on top of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the only place where this underwater mountain range rises above sea level, and the island is gradually splitting apart as the North American and Eurasian plates pull away from each other by a couple of centimeters a year.

hook: Most glaciers are shrinking. This one is growing.
fact: Patagonia's Perito Moreno Glacier is one of the few glaciers on Earth that has remained broadly stable or advancing in recent decades, even as the vast majority of the world's glaciers retreat.

hook: One lake holds more surface area than any other on Earth.
fact: Lake Superior, bordering the US and Canada, is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, covering roughly 82,000 square kilometers.

hook: Astronauts use one desert landmark to help orient themselves from orbit.
fact: Mauritania's Richat Structure, nicknamed the 'Eye of the Sahara,' is a roughly 40-kilometer-wide circular rock formation so distinct it's visible from space — once thought to be an impact crater, it's now understood to be an eroded geological dome.

hook: Thousands of limestone towers rise straight out of the sea in one bay.
fact: Vietnam's Ha Long Bay contains thousands of limestone karst islands and pillars, sculpted over millions of years by water erosion, creating a landscape of steep, forested spires rising from emerald water.

hook: One salt flat turns into the world's largest mirror after it rains.
fact: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat on Earth, and when a thin layer of rainwater covers its surface, it reflects the sky so perfectly that the horizon seems to disappear.

hook: A forest of stone pillars in China inspired a fictional floating mountain range.
fact: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in China features thousands of tall, narrow sandstone pillars carved out over millions of years by erosion, and its otherworldly scenery served as visual inspiration for the floating mountains in the film Avatar.

hook: Some crystals in one Mexican cave are longer than a school bus.
fact: The Cave of Crystals in Naica, Mexico, contains some of the largest natural crystals ever discovered — translucent selenite beams up to around 12 meters long, grown over hundreds of thousands of years in a naturally superheated, mineral-saturated chamber.

hook: A volcano was born in a cornfield and scientists watched the whole thing.
fact: In 1943, a Mexican farmer watched a fissure open in his cornfield and begin spewing ash and lava; within a year it had grown into the 336-meter Paricutin volcano, giving researchers a rare, fully documented record of a volcano's entire life cycle.

hook: Bolivia has two capital cities.
fact: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional and judicial capital, while La Paz — sitting nearly 4,000 meters up in the Andes — serves as the seat of government, hosting the executive and legislative branches.

hook: South Africa runs on three capital cities at once.
fact: Pretoria handles the executive branch, Cape Town hosts parliament, and Bloemfontein is home to the highest court of appeal — a split dating back to a 1910 compromise between rival colonies.

hook: A country's government moved into a brand-new capital almost overnight.
fact: Myanmar's military rulers relocated the capital from Yangon to the purpose-built city of Naypyidaw in 2005, reportedly transferring ministries with little public announcement beforehand.

hook: Nigeria's capital used to be its biggest coastal city.
fact: Nigeria officially moved its capital from Lagos to the newly constructed Abuja in 1991, choosing a more centrally located site meant to feel neutral among the country's many ethnic groups.

hook: Brazil's capital was built from scratch on empty savanna.
fact: Brasília was constructed in under four years and inaugurated in 1960; planner Lúcio Costa laid the city out in a shape often described as resembling an airplane or a bird in flight.

hook: Pakistan swapped its capital for a city built specifically for the job.
fact: Islamabad was constructed in the 1960s to replace Karachi as Pakistan's capital, chosen for its proximity to the military headquarters in nearby Rawalpindi.

hook: Canberra exists because two cities couldn't agree who deserved to be capital.
fact: When Australia federated, Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital, so the government built Canberra as a compromise city roughly halfway between them.

hook: Sri Lanka's official capital isn't the city everyone's heard of.
fact: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, a suburb of Colombo, has been Sri Lanka's official capital since 1982, even though Colombo remains the country's largest city and commercial center.

hook: Ivory Coast's capital isn't its biggest or best-known city.
fact: Yamoussoukro, the birthplace of the country's first president, has been Ivory Coast's official capital since 1983, while Abidjan remains the far larger economic hub.

hook: Tanzania's capital on paper isn't where most of the government actually works.
fact: Dodoma was designated Tanzania's official capital in 1973, but many ministries and embassies remained in Dar es Salaam, the country's largest city, for decades afterward.

hook: Switzerland technically has no official capital.
fact: Bern is only Switzerland's 'federal city' by long-standing custom — the Swiss constitution never formally designates a national capital.

hook: One country's capital has changed its name three times since the 1990s.
fact: Kazakhstan's capital was renamed from Akmola to Astana in 1998, to Nur-Sultan in 2019 in honor of former president Nursultan Nazarbayev, and back to Astana in 2022 after his fall from favor.

hook: A chunk of Russia is completely cut off from the rest of Russia.
fact: Kaliningrad, a Russian region on the Baltic Sea, is separated from the Russian mainland by Poland and Lithuania, making it one of the world's most geopolitically sensitive exclaves.

hook: One of Angola's provinces isn't attached to Angola.
fact: Cabinda, an oil-rich Angolan province, is physically separated from the rest of the country by a strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

hook: Part of Azerbaijan can only be reached by crossing another country.
fact: Nakhchivan, an Azerbaijani exclave, is cut off from the rest of Azerbaijan by Armenian territory, with only narrow borders touching Turkey and Iran.

hook: A Spanish town sits entirely inside France.
fact: Llívia, a small Spanish municipality in the Pyrenees, has been surrounded completely by French territory since a 17th-century treaty accidentally left it out of the land ceded to France.

hook: One border runs straight through people's living rooms.
fact: The Dutch-Belgian border town of Baarle is split into dozens of interlocking enclaves — some buildings have the international boundary marked right across the floor, determining which country's laws apply to which room.

hook: A piece of the United States can only be reached by driving through Canada.
fact: Point Roberts, Washington, sits on a peninsula that dips below the 49th parallel, so the only way to drive there from the rest of the US is through British Columbia.

hook: Part of Oman is walled off from Oman by the UAE.
fact: The Musandam Peninsula, an Omani exclave overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, is separated from the rest of the country by a stretch of United Arab Emirates territory.

hook: The world's most heavily fortified border is also an accidental wildlife sanctuary.
fact: The Korean Demilitarized Zone has seen almost no human development since 1953, letting rare species like cranes and Asiatic black bears thrive in the buffer strip between North and South Korea.

hook: The world's longest international border isn't in Asia or Africa.
fact: The US-Canada border stretches about 8,891 kilometers, including the Alaska section, making it the longest shared land border between any two countries.

hook: Many African borders are perfectly straight lines for a troubling reason.
fact: European colonial powers carved up much of Africa with rulers at conferences like the 1884-85 Berlin Conference, drawing borders that ignored existing ethnic, linguistic, and geographic boundaries entirely.

hook: One capital city is still split in two by an international border.
fact: Nicosia, Cyprus's capital, has remained divided between the internationally recognized Republic of Cyprus and Turkish-controlled Northern Cyprus since 1974, making it the world's last divided capital.

hook: A narrow channel almost triggered a war between two South American neighbors.
fact: Argentina and Chile came close to armed conflict in 1978 over three islands in the Beagle Channel before Pope John Paul II mediated a resolution in 1984.

hook: China runs entirely on a single time zone despite its size.
fact: China spans a longitude that would naturally cover five geographic time zones, but the whole country officially uses just one: Beijing Time.

hook: One country claims more time zones than any other.
fact: France technically covers 12 time zones once its scattered overseas territories are counted, from French Polynesia in the Pacific to French Guiana in South America.
whyItMatters: It's a living reminder of how far colonial-era territory still shapes a modern country's global footprint.

hook: A country moved the International Date Line just to keep its own calendar in sync.
fact: Kiribati shifted its portion of the date line eastward in 1995 so its far-flung islands could share the same date, positioning itself among the first places on Earth to greet each new day.

hook: One country's clocks are set 45 minutes off standard time.
fact: Nepal runs on UTC+5:45, one of only a small handful of places in the world using a time zone offset in 45-minute increments rather than the usual 30 or 60.

hook: The world's most densely packed country is barely bigger than a park.
fact: Monaco is the most densely populated sovereign country on Earth, squeezing tens of thousands of residents onto roughly two square kilometers along the Mediterranean coast.

hook: One country has more empty space per person than almost anywhere else.
fact: Mongolia is the least densely populated sovereign country in the world, with vast stretches of steppe holding only a handful of people per square kilometer.

hook: There's a country believed to have essentially no native-born citizens.
fact: Vatican City has no maternity facilities and almost no permanent families — its population is made up mostly of clergy, Swiss Guards, and officials, so it's believed to have never recorded a birth in its modern history.

hook: One metropolitan area is home to more people than most entire countries.
fact: Greater Tokyo is the largest metropolitan area in the world by population, home to well over 30 million people across its urban sprawl.

hook: Lagos is on track to become one of the largest cities on Earth.
fact: Nigeria's largest city has grown explosively from a modest port town decades ago into one of Africa's biggest megacities, and demographers expect it to keep expanding faster than almost any other major city worldwide.

hook: One territory is more crowded than anywhere else on the planet.
fact: Macau has the highest population density of any territory in the world, packing an enormous number of residents into a strip of land smaller than most cities' downtown districts.

hook: The world's largest island has a population smaller than many small towns.
fact: Greenland covers over two million square kilometers but is home to only around 56,000 people, most of them living along the ice-free southwestern coast.

hook: One island's political status remains one of the world's touchiest geopolitical questions.
fact: Taiwan governs itself with its own military, currency, and elected government, but most countries avoid formally recognizing it as independent to maintain relations with China.
whyItMatters: The ambiguity underpins one of the most closely watched flashpoints in global politics, tied to everything from military alliances to the global semiconductor supply chain.

hook: A country declared independence in 2008 and still isn't fully recognized.
fact: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008; more than 100 countries recognize it, but Serbia, Russia, China, and several EU members, including Spain, still do not.

hook: Africa's last unresolved colonial-era territorial dispute is still unsettled.
fact: Western Sahara remains disputed between Morocco, which controls most of it, and the Polisario Front, which seeks independence for the Sahrawi people — a standoff that has lasted since Spain withdrew in 1975.
whyItMatters: The dispute has stalled development of valuable phosphate deposits and fishing waters and keeps thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps in Algeria.

hook: There's an entire continent that no country owns.
fact: The 1959 Antarctic Treaty set the continent aside for peaceful scientific research and froze all existing territorial claims, meaning no nation legally owns any part of Antarctica.
whyItMatters: As melting ice exposes potential mineral and fishing resources, pressure on that decades-old freeze is expected to grow.

hook: One remote archipelago lets citizens of dozens of countries live there visa-free.
fact: Under the 1920 Svalbard Treaty, citizens of any signatory nation can live and work on the Norwegian-administered archipelago without a visa, a rare arrangement in international law.

hook: Two islands just 3.8 kilometers apart can be nearly a day apart in time.
fact: Big Diomede belongs to Russia and Little Diomede to the United States, separated by a narrow strait — but because the International Date Line runs between them, the islands are often 21 hours apart.

hook: The EU's only land border with Africa runs through two small Spanish cities.
fact: Ceuta and Melilla, Spanish autonomous cities on Morocco's coast, give the European Union its only land borders with the African continent, fenced and heavily patrolled.

hook: Only one national flag isn't a rectangle.
fact: Nepal's flag is made of two stacked triangular pennants, the only national flag in the world with a non-rectangular shape.

hook: One national flag used to be a single solid color with no design at all.
fact: From 1977 to 2011, Libya's flag under Muammar Gaddafi was plain green with no emblem, stripe, or symbol — the only national flag in modern history to feature just one solid color.

hook: One European country is landlocked by other landlocked countries.
fact: Liechtenstein is one of only two 'doubly landlocked' countries in the world — it's entirely surrounded by Switzerland and Austria, both of which are themselves landlocked.

hook: There's only one other doubly landlocked country besides Liechtenstein.
fact: Uzbekistan is the world's other doubly landlocked country, bordered exclusively by Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan.

hook: One country has two foreign heads of state as its co-rulers.
fact: Andorra is jointly ruled by two co-princes: the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell in Spain, a leftover from a medieval feudal agreement that's still technically in force.

hook: One country claims to be the oldest republic still in existence.
fact: San Marino traces its founding to 301 CE, and the tiny microstate maintains it has been continuously self-governing ever since, making it one of the world's oldest surviving states.

hook: One country has had no army for over 75 years.
fact: Costa Rica abolished its military entirely in 1948, redirecting the funds toward education and healthcare, and has had no standing armed forces since.

hook: The world's smallest country has one of its oldest active armies.
fact: The Vatican's Swiss Guard has protected the pope since 1506, making it one of the oldest continuously operating military units still in service anywhere in the world.

hook: There's a country most of the world doesn't officially recognize but functions like one anyway.
fact: Transnistria, a strip of land between Moldova and Ukraine, has run its own government, currency, and army since the early 1990s despite no UN member state recognizing it as independent.
whyItMatters: It remains one of Europe's most enduring 'frozen conflicts,' with Russian troops still stationed there decades after the ceasefire.

hook: One breakaway territory has run its own affairs for over 30 years without recognition.
fact: Somaliland has functioned as a self-governing, de facto independent state since 1991, with its own currency, passport, and elections, yet it's still officially considered part of Somalia by the international community.
whyItMatters: Its stability and strategic location on the Gulf of Aden have drawn quiet foreign investment despite the lack of formal recognition.

hook: The world's most populous country title changed hands recently.
fact: India overtook China to become the world's most populous country around 2023, ending decades of China holding the top spot.

hook: The world's newest widely recognized country is barely a teenager.
fact: South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011 after decades of civil war, making it the youngest country recognized by the United Nations.

hook: One Southeast Asian nation only became independent in this century.
fact: East Timor gained full independence from Indonesia in 2002, following a long Portuguese colonial period and a brutal Indonesian occupation, making it one of Asia's newest nations.

hook: A country changed its name to end a decades-long dispute with a neighbor.
fact: Macedonia officially renamed itself North Macedonia in 2019 under the Prespa Agreement, resolving a long-running naming dispute with Greece that had blocked its path to EU and NATO membership.

hook: One country was renamed by royal decree to avoid confusion with Switzerland.
fact: Swaziland was officially renamed Eswatini in 2018 by King Mswati III, partly to shed a name frequently mixed up with Switzerland on the world stage.

hook: One country split peacefully into two nations in a single year.
fact: Czechoslovakia dissolved into the Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993 without violence, an event so amicable it's often called the 'Velvet Divorce.'

hook: One country's breakup eventually produced seven new nations.
fact: The former Yugoslavia splintered through the 1990s and 2000s into Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Kosovo.

hook: One country's collapse in 1991 created 15 new nations overnight.
fact: The dissolution of the Soviet Union produced 15 newly independent countries, from the Baltic states to the Central Asian republics, reshaping the map of Europe and Asia almost instantly.

hook: Millions of US citizens can't vote for president while living in their own country.
fact: Puerto Ricans are US citizens, but residents of the island cannot vote in presidential elections and have no voting representation in Congress.
whyItMatters: The arrangement fuels an ongoing political debate over statehood, independence, or the territory's current commonwealth status.

hook: Not everyone born under the US flag is a full US citizen.
fact: People born in American Samoa are classified as US nationals rather than full citizens, a unique legal status among all US territories.

hook: Two Danish territories sit outside the European Union.
fact: The Faroe Islands and Greenland are both part of the Kingdom of Denmark, but each has opted to remain outside the European Union even though Denmark itself is a member.

hook: One region has been legally forbidden from having an army for over 150 years.
fact: Åland, an autonomous, Swedish-speaking region of Finland, has been demilitarized under international treaty since the 19th century, a status reaffirmed multiple times since.

hook: Two countries still dispute a set of islands that sparked a war in 1982.
fact: The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic that Argentina claims as the Islas Malvinas, a dispute that escalated into armed conflict in 1982.

hook: One airport's runway is crossed by the main road into town.
fact: Gibraltar's airport runway intersects Winston Churchill Avenue, the territory's principal road, so traffic barriers stop cars whenever a plane needs to take off or land.

hook: Two Chinese cities run on entirely different legal and economic systems than the mainland.
fact: Hong Kong and Macau operate under a 'one country, two systems' framework, retaining their own currencies, legal systems, and border controls separate from mainland China.

hook: One island is legally off-limits to outsiders to protect its residents.
fact: North Sentinel Island in India's Andaman chain is home to the Sentinelese, an isolated tribe that has resisted outside contact for thousands of years; Indian law bans anyone from approaching the island.
whyItMatters: The restriction exists largely to protect the tribe from diseases they have no immunity to, which could wipe out the population on contact.

hook: One British territory has one of the smallest populations of any place on Earth.
fact: The Pitcairn Islands, settled originally by mutineers from HMS Bounty, are home to only around 40 people today, making it one of the least populated jurisdictions in the world.

hook: The most remote inhabited place on Earth is a tiny volcanic archipelago.
fact: Tristan da Cunha, a British territory in the South Atlantic, sits more than 2,400 kilometers from the nearest inhabited land, making it the most isolated permanently inhabited archipelago on the planet.

hook: A WWII sea fort declared itself an independent country.
fact: Sealand, a former anti-aircraft platform built off the English coast during World War II, has operated as a self-declared micronation since 1967, complete with its own flag, currency, and passports — though no country recognizes it.

hook: One organization issues its own passports and license plates without owning any territory.
fact: The Sovereign Military Order of Malta holds permanent observer status at the United Nations and issues its own diplomatic passports and vehicle plates from its headquarters in Rome, despite having no territory of its own.

hook: One country has never bothered to name an official capital.
fact: Nauru, the world's third-smallest country, has no officially designated capital; government offices are simply clustered in the district of Yaren.

hook: One tiny Pacific nation makes real money off its internet domain.
fact: Tuvalu licenses its country-code domain, .tv, to media and streaming companies worldwide, generating a meaningful stream of national revenue for one of the smallest economies on Earth.
whyItMatters: With rising seas threatening to submerge much of the low-lying nation, digital revenue like this has become an unusually important lifeline.

hook: One country formally asked the world to stop calling it by its English name.
fact: Turkey requested in 2022 that the United Nations and other bodies use 'Türkiye' instead of 'Turkey' in official contexts, partly to distance the name from the English word for the bird.

hook: Thousands of people once lived in pockets of one country stranded inside another.
fact: Until 2015, India and Bangladesh shared the world's most complex enclave system, with over 100 tiny pockets of each country's territory scattered inside the other, some containing enclaves of their own within enclaves.
whyItMatters: A 2015 land-swap agreement finally exchanged the territories, ending decades in which many residents lived effectively without full access to citizenship, schools, or utilities.

hook: Two cities compete for the title of the world's southernmost city.
fact: Argentina's Ushuaia has long marketed itself as the southernmost city on Earth, but Chile's Puerto Williams, reclassified from a town to a city in 2019, actually sits farther south.

hook: The world's northernmost town with year-round residents is deep in the Arctic.
fact: Longyearbyen, on Norway's Svalbard archipelago, is home to roughly 2,400 people and is the northernmost settlement on Earth with a permanent civilian population.

hook: There's a fictional island at the exact center of the world map.
fact: Null Island is a joke placeholder for coordinates 0° latitude, 0° longitude — a point in the Atlantic Ocean where mapping software often dumps broken location data, prompting NOAA to actually anchor a monitoring buoy there.

hook: 'Holland' isn't actually the name of the whole country.
fact: Holland technically refers to just two of the Netherlands' twelve provinces, North Holland and South Holland; the Dutch government even launched a campaign in 2020 to retire 'Holland' as a nickname for the whole country.

hook: One country is literally named after its location on the globe.
fact: Ecuador is the Spanish word for 'equator,' and the line itself runs just north of the capital, Quito, where a monument marks the crossing.

hook: One landlocked country has six different neighbors.
fact: Chad, entirely landlocked in central Africa, shares borders with Libya, Sudan, the Central African Republic, Cameroon, Nigeria, and Niger.

hook: Two countries are tied for having the most land neighbors on Earth.
fact: China and Russia each border 14 other countries, more than any other nation, a reflection of their sheer size and sprawling frontiers.

hook: The world's smallest country has its own tiny railway.
fact: Vatican City is connected to Italy's rail network by a short spur of track roughly 300 meters long, often cited as one of the shortest state railways in the world.
